steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Classical conditioning (Pavlov): learning by association. A neutral stimulus becomes associated with an unconditioned stimulus, producing a conditioned response. Pavlov's dogs: bell (NS) paired with food (UCS) -> salivation (UCR). After conditioning: bell alone (CS) -> salivation (CR). Explains phobias and emotional responses.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Operant conditioning (Skinner): learning by consequences. Positive reinforcement: adding something pleasant to increase behaviour (reward). Negative reinforcement: removing something unpleasant to increase behaviour (taking painkillers removes pain). Punishment: adding something unpleasant to decrease behaviour. Skinner's Box: rats pressed a lever for food (positive reinforcement).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Social Learning Theory (Bandura): we learn by observing others. Key processes: attention (notice the behaviour), retention (remember it), reproduction (ability to copy it), motivation (want to copy it - influenced by vicarious reinforcement). Bandura's Bobo doll study: children who saw an aggressive model were significantly more aggressive.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Mediational processes in SLT distinguish it from pure behaviourism: SLT acknowledges cognitive processes (attention, retention, motivation) mediate between stimulus and response. This makes SLT more comprehensive than traditional behaviourism.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Describe classical conditioning and operant conditioning, using examples from psychological research. | Explain Bandura's Social Learning Theory and evaluate how well it accounts for observational learning. | Compare the behaviourist approach with the cognitive approach, evaluating their relative contributions.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Classical conditioning = ASSOCIATION (Pavlov's dogs). Operant conditioning = CONSEQUENCES (Skinner's rats). SLT process: ARRM - Attention, Retention, Reproduction, Motivation. We learn by OBSERVING, not just doing. Behaviourism = observable behaviour only. Cognitive = mental processes. SLT bridges both.
